Title: The Finnish Footballer: Simon Enqvist's Journey to IFK Mariehamn

In the picturesque town of Mariehamn, Finland, nestled in the heart of the Åland Islands, a talented young footballer named Simon Enqvist was making waves in the world of Finnish football. With a passion that burned brighter than the Nordic sun, Simon's dedication to the beautiful game would eventually lead him to don the iconic blue and white jersey of IFK Mariehamn, one of Finland's most beloved association football clubs. Growing up in the Åland Islands, Simon was surrounded by the rugged beauty of the Baltic Sea and the rich cultural heritage of his native Finland. It was here, amidst the windswept coastlines and rolling hills, that Simon's love affair with football began. As a young boy, he would spend hours kicking the ball around with his friends, dreaming of one day becoming a professional footballer. As Simon's skills improved, so did his reputation. He began to make a name for himself in local youth leagues, catching the attention of coaches and scouts from across the region. It wasn't long before Simon's talent and hard work earned him a spot on the roster of IFK Mariehamn's youth academy. Under the guidance of experienced coaches and trainers, Simon honed his craft, refining his technique and developing a deep understanding of the game. He quickly became a standout player, known for his lightning-quick speed, razor-sharp instincts, and unwavering commitment to his teammates. As Simon matured, so did his game. He began to make appearances for IFK Mariehamn's reserve team, where he continued to impress with his skill and tenacity. It was only a matter of time before he would be called up to the senior squad, and in 2018, that moment finally arrived. On a crisp autumn evening, Simon Enqvist made his professional debut for IFK Mariehamn, taking to the pitch in front of a packed crowd at the Wiklöf Holding Arena. The excitement was palpable as Simon, donning the number 17 jersey, took his place alongside his new teammates. The evidence was clear: Simon Enqvist had officially become a member of IFK Mariehamn's senior squad. The club's website, social media channels, and local newspapers all confirmed the news, as did the Finnish Football Association's official records.

{"relevant": true, "cards": [{"entity": "", "sense": "", "answer": "", "as_of": "", "claim_kind": "", "attributed_to": "", "evidence": "", "claim": ""}]}

"relevant": false if the document is about some other topic and is of no use for the question; then "cards" is [].
"cards": one card for each answer the document itself gives to the question. Usually that is one card. It is several cards if the document gives several answers, such as a list of names: one card each. It is [] if the document gives no answer. The question may fit several things that share a name: whichever of them this document is about, report its answer. If the document only says that some answer is wrong, write no card for that answer.

The fields of a card:
- "entity": who or what this answer is about, as specifically as the document identifies it: the full name, plus the details the document gives that tell it apart from others with the same name (what kind of thing it is, profession or role, nationality or place, years, creator, other names), even where the question does not ask about them. At most about 25 words.
- "sense": which event, edition, version, condition, place or measure the answer refers to, if the document says; otherwise "not stated".
- "answer": the answer, copied from the document as it is written there, and short: a full name, a date, a number with its unit, or a short phrase. For a yes-or-no question, "yes" or "no".
- "as_of": the date at which this was true, if the document says; otherwise "not stated".
- "claim_kind": "factual", or "opinion" for a judgment, a recommendation or a contested finding.
- "attributed_to": who or what the document says this comes from, such as a census, a study or a named person, if it says; otherwise "not stated".
- "evidence": the sentence of the document that gives the answer, copied word for word. Two sentences if one is not enough.
- "claim": one sentence that states the answer on its own and names the entity.

Inside a JSON string, write a double quote as \".
